thread_analysis.thread_summary: This thread covers FY26 Bluetooth SIG certification for [COMPANY] Sony's TV body and remote control products, handled as two separate registration projects. For the TV (OS version upgrade of a 3-year-old registration): the consultant confirmed RF test report reuse was valid since RF hardware was unchanged, then identified ICS inter-layer inconsistencies in the proposed reference QDID (Q325703), proposed using a Subset QDID (Q333791) to avoid triggering the post-July 2024 ~300-item LL Test Plan requirement, and quoted ¥400,000 (proxy registration + Compliance Folder only, no new testing). For the remote control (new BLE HID product): the consultant identified that QPRDv4 takes effect November 10, 2025, adding IOPT interoperability tests; by completing SIG server registration by November 9 (leveraging the new 180-day advance publication date feature), all RF/profile tests are exempt at ¥400,000 total; after November 10, IOPT tests add ¥200,000. The thread also includes an internal note confirming the Core Spec version in the registration will be v5.2 (from the referenced QDID D049426), not v5.4 as the customer specified in their RFQ.
all_questions_found: Can the existing RF/RFPHY test report from a 3-year-old registration be reused for an OS version upgrade listing when RF hardware is unchanged?
The reference QDID has ICS inter-layer inconsistencies - can we use a Subset QDID to avoid triggering ~300-item LL test requirements under the 2024 registration system?
QPRDv4 takes effect November 10, 2025 with new IOPT test requirements - can we avoid them by registering before the deadline, and does the 180-day advance publication date feature help?
The customer specified Core Spec v5.4 in the RFQ - will the registration actually use v5.4?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Two advanced technical issues are central: (1) Post-July 2024 registration system rule: any LL ICS change triggers a full LL Test Plan with ~300 test items - this makes fixing ICS inter-layer inconsistencies via ICS modifications impractical, and instead requires finding a Subset QDID that naturally avoids the inconsistency. (2) QPRD deadline-based test exemption: QPRDv4 effective November 10, 2025 added IOPT tests; the 180-day advance publication date feature allows a product to be registered (and locked into current test requirements) before its launch date, making 'register early, launch later' a viable cost-reduction strategy. RF test report reuse is valid when the wireless module and RF specs are genuinely unchanged across registrations. Core Spec version in a registration is dictated by the referenced QDIDs, not the applicant's stated version.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: QDID selection must account for ICS inter-layer consistency, not just RF class compatibility. When a parent QDID has inconsistencies, search its available Subsets for one that avoids the problem. When a QPRD version change deadline is approaching, proactively present two quotes (pre-deadline vs. post-deadline) and highlight the cost savings. Always verify Core Spec version from the QDID reference chain before quoting and inform the customer of any discrepancy with their stated version.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Using a QDID with inter-layer inconsistencies without checking Subsets can result in a registration being blocked or triggering an unforeseen ~300-item test plan. Missing a QPRD deadline can cost the customer hundreds of thousands of yen in avoidable test fees. Failing to flag a Core Spec version discrepancy from the RFQ can lead to customer confusion about their certified specification level.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When assessing a new registration referencing older QDIDs: (1) Check for ICS inter-layer inconsistencies in the reference QDID and look for Subsets that avoid them; (2) Under the post-July 2024 system, avoid LL ICS modifications as they trigger impractically large test plans; (3) Monitor QPRD version effective dates proactively and present deadline-based quotes to customers; (4) Use the 180-day advance publication date feature as a scheduling tool for 'register before deadline, launch later' strategies; (5) Always cross-check Core Spec version from the QDID reference chain against what the customer specified.
